image_description: A grey whale breaching vertically out of the ocean, displaying its ventral side (throat and belly) with characteristic mottled grey skin and white barnacle patches. The head is angled upward showing the arched rostrum from below. In the background, there are small boats with people observing, providing scale reference against the massive whale body.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Head is relatively short with arched rostrum and two blowholes on top.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image shows the ventral (underside) view of the whale's head during a breach. Blowholes are located on the dorsal surface and are anatomically impossible to see from this angle. This is an occlusion/viewpoint issue, not an absence of the feature.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey to greyish-black with distinctive white patches from barnacles and whale lice.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin clearly displays the characteristic mottled grey coloration with distinct white patches consistent with barnacle coverage on the head and throat area.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: No dorsal fin present; multiple dorsal knuckles along posterior back.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The dorsal side of the whale is facing away from the camera or submerged. The posterior back and dorsal knuckles are completely occluded by the viewing angle and water.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Robust spindle-shaped body of enormous proportions.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: While partially submerged, the visible portion of the body demonstrates the robust, thick proportions characteristic of a grey whale. Scale comparison with background boats confirms enormous size.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin is mottled grey with white patches created by barnacles.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible body surface clearly shows mottled grey skin with white barnacle patches extending from head to torso.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Baleen plates are cream-colored, densely packed in numerous rows along each side.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The mouth is closed and baleen plates are internal structures not visible in this breaching pose.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Flippers (pectoral fins) are broad and paddle-shaped, remarkably elongated relative to body size.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: Pectoral fins are not visible in this specific breaching angle - they appear to be submerged or obscured by the body position.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail flukes are broad with smooth trailing edge and central notch.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail flukes are completely underwater and not visible in this vertical breach shot.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Skin texture is rough with callosities.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible skin surface shows rough texture with raised areas consistent with callosities and barnacle attachments on the throat and body.
